methodological_rigor.justification: Single-center retrospective cohort of 118 patients (90 ≤3cm, 28 >3cm) who underwent TACE-pRFA for early-stage HCC ≤5cm. Median follow-up 31 months. Univariable and multivariable Cox regression analyses performed. Appropriate comparison of baseline characteristics between groups. Limitations: small sample size, single-center design, retrospective with inherent selection bias, no randomization.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Individual cohort study (LoE 2b) assessing combined TACE-pRFA for early-stage HCC, clinically relevant intervention for tumors 3-5cm where single modality has limitations. Direct applicability to hepatocellular carcinoma treatment strategy selection. However, findings primarily confirmatory of previous single-center studies rather than paradigm-shifting.

reporting_quality.justification: Observational study with STROBE principles evident (patient selection flowchart, baseline characteristics, outcome definition using Kaplan-Meier PFS). Treatment procedures detailed (TACE/pRFA technical specifications). Complications classified per Society of Interventional Radiology guidelines. No data sharing statement; limited reproducibility details for external centers.

novelty_literature.justification: Confirmatory study evaluating combination TACE-pRFA for early HCC; incremental confirmation of prior similar single-center studies with comparable results. Main contribution is comparison of ≤3cm versus >3cm subgroups rather than novel therapeutic approach. Limited mechanistic or discovery-level novelty.

writing_presentation.justification: Clear organization with well-structured methods, detailed TACE/pRFA procedures, comprehensive result presentation with Kaplan-Meier curves stratified by tumor size and other factors. Discussion contextualizes findings among competing locoregional therapies (SBRT, microwave ablation, surgical resection) and positions TACE-pRFA appropriately.

key_strengths: Clear clinical question: comparative effectiveness of TACE-pRFA stratified by tumor size (≤3cm vs >3cm) for early-stage HCC
Comprehensive safety assessment: zero procedure-related mortality/disability/major complications; manageable discomfort in 67.8% of patients
Appropriate statistical analysis: Kaplan-Meier survival curves, univariable/multivariable Cox regression identifying maximum tumor diameter as independent PFS predictor (HR 2.87, p=0.023)
Detailed technical descriptions enabling clinical comparison with other treatment modalities
Reasonable outcomes: median PFS 35.0 months (95% CI 24.3-45.7); superior to previously reported pRFA-alone outcomes
key_concerns: Single-center, small sample (n=118, only 28 in >3cm group) introducing selection bias and limiting generalizability
Retrospective design without propensity matching or other adjustment for treatment allocation bias
Primarily confirmatory results replicating findings of prior similar studies without substantial novelty
TACE-pRFA shows 57.6% recurrence rate and intrahepatic distant recurrence in 45.8%; discussion acknowledges but incompletely addresses high progression rates
No external validation; no data sharing statement limiting reproducibility
chief_reviewer.rationale: Competent single-center retrospective study with reasonable safety profile and modest clinical contribution. Appropriate for Tier 3 (4-9.9 JIF). Minor revisions should address power calculations and comparative effectiveness claims.
